question: Does footnote *4's clause 'during the irrigation season when irrigation return flows in the lower Animas Ditch likely discharge back to the Animas River when most sensitive juvenile life forms are likely to be present in the receiving water and colder ambient temperatures might adversely affect treatment processes' establish applicability conditions that must be satisfied before the once-per-term Whole Effluent Toxicity monitoring obligation attaches, or does it only specify when the otherwise-required once-per-term test must be scheduled?
semantic_arguments: permit effective date and the timing of the first springtime after that date relative to Federal FY2025
whether irrigation season occurred during the relevant period
whether irrigation return flows in the lower Animas Ditch likely discharged back to the Animas River during that period
whether the juvenile life-form sensitivity and ambient temperature conditions described in footnote *4 were met
relationship between the unconditional-sounding 'Once per permit term' requirement and the conditional 'when' language in footnote *4
notes: A scheduling-only reading treats WET monitoring as required once per permit term with preferred timing; an applicability reading treats the ecological and hydrological conditions as preconditions. That distinction changes whether WET monitoring was required during FY2025 (Purpose B) and whether absent WET results represent conditional monitoring not required versus required monitoring lacking adequate evidence (Purpose C).
